item.title: AI Security
item.description: <p>Two weeks ago, I attended the <a href="https://unpromptedcon.org/">[un]prompted</a> AI security conference in San Francisco. It was an excellent event: three days of very dense talks about all aspects of AI security. (My talk was about integrous AI, and I will post it when it is online.)</p> <p>AI security can be divided into three broad topics. It&#8217;s important for researchers to understand which one they are working on. And it&#8217;s important for us as a community to work on them all. They are: security of AI, security with AI, and security from AI. [un]prompted had good talks about all three...</p>
item.dc:creator: Bruce Schneier

item.title: Hackers Hide Linux Backdoor in Control Web Panel Server to Execute Commands Without Logs
item.description:
A backdoor has been found hiding in the web server that runs Control Web Panel (CWP), a free panel for managing Linux hosting servers, researchers at QiAnXin's XLab said this week.
The backdoored web server executes commands that attackers send via web requests, and those requests never appear in its access logs. Installing it takes root access, so the attackers must already control the server.
